subject: Post-demo: QuantArc model shortlist, benchmarks, next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Green <ellis.green@quantarc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: QuantArc model shortlist, benchmarks, next steps

Hi Ellis — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our demo + the recommended next steps so your team can review. I included a short model shortlist, the benchmark output, and the prompt set we used for the quality checks (attached).

High-level summary
- Goal: ~95% answer accuracy on your support QA set, <250 ms p95 latency for short queries, and predictable unit cost under $0.10 per 1k tokens for the steady-state workload.
- Demo takeaway: We see two practical paths depending on tolerance for latency vs. cost: a smaller quantized variant for lower cost (higher risk on edge-case quality) and a higher-capacity model for better quality at higher cost/latency.

Recommended shortlist (prioritized)
1) rw-instruct-8b-q4f16 (Recommended starter) — Rationale: best cost/quality balance in our PoC prompts; median p95 ~180 ms on a 4090 pool, expected cost ~$0.06/1k tokens. Good for customer-facing responses where latency matters.
2) rw-13b-plat-8bit (Quality-first, moderate latency) — Rationale: ~5–8% lift on correctness for long-context troubleshooting prompts; p95 ~320 ms; cost ~$0.18/1k tokens. Good if you want to reduce hallucination risk on complex chains.
3) open-70b-compat (Fallback/high-quality) — Rationale: best-in-class quality on our evals but higher latency (~700 ms p95) and cost (~$0.75/1k tokens). Suggested for batch re-ranking / overnight jobs, less ideal for real-time chat.

Key caveats we spotted
- Regression sensitivity: A small change to the prompt templates (particularly the system-level instruction) produced 6–9% swings in entity extraction accuracy on a 200-sample holdout. We included the prompt_set_v1.md so you can replay locally.
- Prefix caching: For conversational flows with repeated question stems we saw 30–40% token-cost savings when caching KV prefix between turns; this requires a small SDK change on your side (we can provide a snippet).

Attachments (attached to this message)
- quantarc_poc_benchmarks_20270401.csv (detailed latency and accuracy by prompt)
- prompt_set_v1.md (the prompt templates used in the test harness)
- model_shortlist_rationale.pdf (slide with charts and per-model decision notes)

Suggested next steps (mutual action plan)
- Review shortlist + prompt set with the engineering and security teams (you) — reply with any immediate concerns by EOD Tue 4/5.
- Redwood to run a 1-week dedicated-run (hosted) with your top 2 models on a 50k-query slice — we will provide exact metrics and a cost estimate. (Action: Karthik to schedule; ETA 4/6 start)
- Procurement/security: if onboarding looks good, we can provide a SOW and the SOC2 evidence pack for QuantArc to review.

I'll follow up with Ben (pricing) and Marissa (CS/PoC ops) below to get a costed plan in your hands.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Ellis Green <ellis.green@quantarc.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@quantarc.com
Date: 2027-04-01T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: QuantArc model shortlist, benchmarks, next steps

Karthik — thanks, this is helpful. A couple of quick questions from our side: 
- Can you confirm where the data for real-time inference would be stored during the PoC and what retention policy applies? Our security team will want to know whether sessions are persisted beyond 7 days.
- On the quantized 8b option: do you have examples of failure modes where it drops below acceptable threshold? Specifically worried about multi-turn troubleshooting prompts.

Procurement is cc'd here to start the commercial thread — they may ask for a standard NDAs/SOW before the PoC. We also need to confirm whether Redwood can host in AWS us-west-2 (we prefer that region).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Ellis
Director, Platform Engineering — QuantArc

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Green <ellis.green@quantarc.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: QuantArc model shortlist, benchmarks, next steps (pricing + hosting notes)

Ellis / Karthik — quick pricing and hosting clarification from my side.

Hosting/region
- We can run the PoC in AWS us-west-2 (hosted) with full VPC peering and customer-managed keys. Data retention for ephemeral inference logs is configurable; default demo retention is 7 days. If QuantArc needs shorter retention or zero-retention, we can turn off logs for the PoC (limited observability).

Pricing (estimates for PoC traffic: 50k queries, ~20 tokens avg response)
- rw-instruct-8b-q4f16 (hosted) — est cost: $280 for the PoC run + infra fee; latency p95 ~180ms.
- rw-13b-plat-8bit (hosted) — est cost: $840 for PoC; latency p95 ~320ms.
- Dedicated option (monthly committed) — if you move to a Reserved pool we can get unit costs down ~30% and p95 latency more stable (we would need a 3-month commit).

Failure mode notes (answering Ellis' question)
- The 8b quantized variant tends to degrade on long, deeply nested instruction chains (example: multi-step resolution that refers back 5+ turns). In our tests this showed up as wrong entity mapping ~6% of the time. The 13b model reduces that to ~1–2% but at higher cost.

Next ops items I can own:
- Draft a short SOW + demo-priced quote for the 1-week PoC (will include region, retention, and mini-SLA). ETA: 2027-04-03 EOD.
- If you want dedicated capacity numbers, I can include 1-month and 3-month reserved-cost scenarios.

cc Marissa for PoC runbook and engineering checklist.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Ellis Green <ellis.green@quantarc.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@quantarc.com
Date: 2027-04-03T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: QuantArc model shortlist, benchmarks, next steps

Thanks Ben / Karthik — that scope looks good. Procurement will review the SOW and confirm whether they need an NDA first. We are happy to start with the rw-instruct-8b-q4f16 for the PoC and evaluate the 13b for a second pass. Please go ahead and send the SOW + PoC schedule; proposed kickoff week = 2027-04-06.

Also, Ellis to Ellis note to our security team: we're ok with 7-day retention for the PoC but please escalate if you need a shorter window.

I'll look out for the SOW.

Ellis
Director, Platform Engineering — QuantArc
